data.title: CoreWeave co-founder discloses bond purchase, says he will hold until maturity
data.description:
CoreWeave co-founder and Chief Strategy Officer Brian Venturo disclosed late on Wednesday that he purchased some of the company's unsecured bonds and intends to hold them until maturity.

"Last week, I purchased $30 million in face value of CoreWeave’s unsecured bonds," Venturo wrote in a post on LinkedIn. "I intend to hold them to maturity on October 1, 2031. When we started CoreWeave, I couldn’t have imagined the scale of what our customers are building with us today. I believe in their work, and I’m proud of the team we’ve built to support it. I’ve never been more confident in CoreWeave."

Shares of the Livingston, N.J.-based company rose 5.8% in premarket trading on Thursday.

CoreWeave's debt has seen sharp drops in prices lately as investors become concerned about the neocloud industry's ability to survive if the artificial intelligence spending boom were to slow down.

Earlier this month, it was reported that CoreWeave was planning to raise at least $4B through an investment-grade loan, with Morgan Stanley and Mitsubishi UFJ Financial Group leading the potential financing. The proposed financing is expected to follow a structure backed by semiconductor chips and related customer contracts, allowing CoreWeave to borrow at a lower cost than through the high-yield debt market. The company has increasingly relied on asset-backed financing to fund its AI infrastructure expansion.

The move comes after CoreWeave raised its full-year revenue forecast, helping ease investor concerns about its debt-heavy business. The company reported third-quarter revenue of $3.66B, up 168% year-over-year, and raised its 2026 revenue outlook to between $13B and $13.3B.

CoreWeave CEO Michael Intrator also recently indicated that he has cancelled his 10b5-1 plan. A 10b5-1 is a pre-arranged stock trading plan that allows corporate insiders—such as CEOs and board members—to sell or buy company shares on a fixed schedule.

data.title: Financial stocks lift Sri Lankan shares marginally higher
data.description:
Sri Lankan shares closed slightly higher on Thursday, led by financial stocks.

  • The CSE All-Share index settled up 0.66% at 21,543.12 points.

  • Commercial Bank of Ceylon and Hatton National Bank were the biggest lift for the index, up 0.94% and 0.95%, respectively, on the day.

  • Trading volume on the exchange fell to 53.8 million shares from 95.2 million shares in the previous session.

  • The equity market's turnover dipped to 1.73 billion Sri Lankan rupees ($5.20 million) from 1.93 billion rupees in the previous session, according to exchange data.

  • Foreign investors were net sellers, offloading stocks worth 134.7 million rupees, while domestic investors were net buyers, purchasing shares worth 1.69 billion rupees, the data showed.

data.title: TSMC, Samsung Reportedly Suspend Some Chip Deliveries To Chinese Customers Amid New US Export Rules
data.description:
Key points:
  • Deliveries are paused while the chipmakers apply for licenses from the US Commerce Department, FT reported.
  • The new U.S. rules close a route that let Chinese chip designers obtain high-performance processors through independent packaging and testing firms.
  • Smartphone chip licenses would likely be approved, though the process could cause manufacturing delays, the report said.

Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co. (TSM) and Samsung Electronics have reportedly suspended shipments of certain semiconductors to Chinese customers following new U.S. export restrictions aimed at limiting Beijing’s access to advanced artificial intelligence chips,

The chipmakers informed Chinese customers in recent days that deliveries would be paused while they apply for licenses from the US Commerce Department, the Financial Times reported Thursday, citing multiple people briefed on the matter.

​Stocktwits reached out to both Samsung and TSMC for comment but had not received a response from either company at the time of publication.

New Rules Close Chip Supply Route

The US Commerce Department’s Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) introduced new licensing requirements on Monday for certain advanced chips produced using American technology.

According to the publication, the changes close a pathway that allowed Chinese chip designers to obtain high-performance processors through independent packaging and testing companies.

​Previously, these companies could verify that chip designs fell outside US export restrictions, enabling shipments without direct government approval. The new requirements remove that route for affected Chinese customers, the report said.

​The restrictions add pressure to China’s technology sector, which is already facing rising memory chip prices and capacity constraints at domestic suppliers such as Semiconductor Manufacturing International Corporation.

Smartphone Chip Deliveries Also Affected

TSMC and Samsung have also notified consumer electronics customers of shipment suspensions, per the report. The new regulations eliminate exemptions previously used to establish that certain advanced chips were intended for non-AI applications, including smartphones.

Samsung’s Chinese customers include Baidu’s AI data-center chip unit Kunlun and TikTok parent ByteDance, both of which have sought alternative chip supplies amid shortages of Nvidia processors in China, the FT reported, but it did not establish that shipments to either company were specifically suspended.

Meanwhile, TSMC manufactures smartphone processors for Chinese companies including Xiaomi, Oppo and Vivo.

An indutry insider told the FT that US authorities would likely approve licenses for consumer smartphone chips, but the licensing process could cause significant manufacturing delays. The timing of regulatory approvals remains uncertain, leaving manufacturers without clarity on when affected shipments can resume.

Retail Sentiment Around TSM Stock

On Stocktwits, retail investors’ sentiment around TSM stock flipped to ‘bearish’ from ‘neutral’ a day ago.

So far in 2026, TSM shares have gained more than 13%, while Samsung’s South Korea-listed shares have surged over 53%.

In comparison, the Direxion Daily Semiconductor Bull 3X ETF (SOXL), which holds TSMC shares, and the Roundhill Memory ETF (DRAM), which holds Samsung shares, have risen more than 4% and 41% year-to-date, respectively.

data.title: Temu Owner Reports Flat Profit, Revenue as Challenges Continue
data.description:
(11:32 GMT) *PDD Holdings 3Q Revenue Flat on Year >PDD
(11:34 GMT) *PDD Holdings 3Q Profit Rose 0.7% on Year >PDD
(12:27 GMT) Temu Owner Reports Flat Profit, Revenue as Challenges Continue

By Tracy Qu

The Chinese owner of bargain-shopping app Temu posted flat earnings as it continued to deal with subdued consumer sentiment at home and regulatory pressures abroad.

Still, the results ended a string of profit declines for PDD Holdings, whose profitability has been under pressure in recent quarters it strengthens its e-commerce ecosystem. The company has also faced challenges in overseas markets amid tightened regulatory requirements and geopolitical tensions.

The company behind Temu and Chinese platform Pinduoduo on Thursday said net profit edged 0.7% higher from a year earlier to 29.54 billion yuan, equivalent to $4.43 billion. Revenue was little changed at 108.34 billion yuan.

Analysts had expected net profit of 24.81 billion yuan on revenue of 115.67 billion yuan, according to a FactSet consensus.

"We remain in a strategic investment phase, focused on strengthening supply-chain capabilities and supporting our merchants," said Jun Liu, vice president of finance.

PDD's American depositary receipts rose nearly 9% premarket, pointing to brightening investor sentiment. Appetite for the Nasdaq-listed company has waned as sentiment on tech companies weakened, leaving PDD's stock down by about one third this year.

Citi analysts pointed to Temu's shrinking user base, with Europe leading the decline as PDD faces tighter regulations in the bloc. Temu's global monthly active users fell 17.8% on iOS and 11.2% on Android in September, Citi said, citing third-party estimates.

Adding to its headwinds, the European Commission earlier this week said measures Temu put in place to tackle illegal products sold on its platform were insufficient, including what it called a "weak" content moderation system and ineffective sanctions. A PDD spokesperson said the company disagrees with the commission's view and will respond to the findings.

Meanwhile, back home, subdued consumer sentiment is weighing on Pinduoduo's performance. Total retail sales of consumer goods grew just 1.1% during the first nine months of 2026, official data showed. Sales for this year's Singles' Day--China's biggest online-shopping event of the year--rose 4.8% from last year, according to data provider Syntun.

data.title: Polymarket Indicates 29% Chance Anthropic's Market Cap Lands Above $1.5 Trillion — WSJ
data.description:
By Rebecca Feng

Bets on prediction-markets platform Polymarket give a 21% chance that Anthropic's market capitalization by the end of today will land between $1.5 trillion and $1.75 trillion, and 8% odds that it would land between $1.75 trillion and $2.75 trillion.

Put together, the bets imply a roughly 29% chance of a market debut that would see the stock pop 36%, and an almost 80% chance of shares rising 14% above the IPO price on the first day.

Anthropic's shares were priced at $83 apiece at the company's initial public offering, a level that would put the Claude maker's market cap at around $1.1 trillion based on a basic share count. This doesn't include so-called fully diluted shares which would include stock yet to be issued via options. (On that basis, the company's value at the IPO price is around $1.5 trillion.)

The Polymarket bet looks at Anthropic's market cap based on the basic share-count method. Anthropic's shares are trading 25% above its IPO price in the gray market, indicating a share price of $105 apiece, or a market cap of around $1.375 trillion.

Polymarket has a data partnership with Dow Jones, the publisher of The Wall Street Journal.

This item is part of a Wall Street Journal live coverage event. The full stream can be found by searching P/WSJL (WSJ Live Coverage).

data.title: Johnson Matthey says demand for pollution filters used at AI data centres outstrips supply
data.description:
Key points:
  • Cormetech acquisition closed in July
  • CEO Liam Condon says equipment additions are needed to expand output
  • Data centres are increasingly turning to wind turbines to ease pressure on power grids

By Nithyashree R B and Yadarisa Shabong

Demand for pollution filters used at AI data centres is far outstripping supply, Johnson Matthey CEO Liam Condon said on Thursday, as the company raised its annual sales expectations for its stationary emissions control businesses.

Data centres, whose construction is surging notably in the US as big tech companies pour money into AI computing and spurring demand for power, are increasingly turning to gas turbines to overcome grid constraints. That is also boosting demand for emission controls that need to be installed to meet regulations.

Britain's Johnson Matthey, which mainly makes pollution filters for cars and trucks, completed its acquisition in July of Cormetech, a US-based maker of catalysts that strip nitrogen oxides from gas-turbine exhaust.

"For some time, we've had to turn away potential customers because demand far outstrips supply at this stage of the market," Condon told Reuters after the company reported higher first-half operating profit.

Condon said on an analyst call that Johnson Matthey has the manufacturing capacity to boost production, but would need to buy more machines and dryers to make more products.

The market for selective catalytic reduction (SCR) systems — which reduce emissions — is worth about $1 billion and is expected to grow 10% to 15% annually over the next five to seven years mainly driven by data centres, Condon told Reuters in June after the company announced the Cormetech deal.

Other players in the SCR market include Belgium's Umicore , Austria's CERAM and parts of German ​chemicals group BASF .

Johnson Matthey raised its annual sales expectation for Cormetech and its Clean Air Solutions business, which serves the stationary emissions market in the marine, industrial and utilities sectors, to more than £250 million ($328 million), from more than £200 million previously.

The company will report the two businesses as its Clean Power segment from full year 2026/27.

($1 = 0.7614 pounds)

data.title: Siemens Energy signs 200-MW electrolyser deal for Swedish e-SAF site
data.description:
November 19 (Renewables Now) - Siemens Energy AG (ETR:ENR) has been tapped to supply around 200 MW of electrolysis capacity for Alby PtX’s planned sustainable aviation fuel (e-SAF) plant in Sweden, which is designed to produce 66,000 tonnes of e-SAF per year.

Selected as the electrolyser original equipment manufacturer (OEM), the German firm will initially deliver a basic engineering design package. Final equipment procurement remains subject to a positive final investment decision (FID) by Alby PtX.

The e-SAF project, planned in the municipality of Ange, will use renewable electricity to produce hydrogen using Siemens Energy's Elyzer P-300 proton exchange membrane (PEM) technology. The green hydrogen will then be combined with captured CO2 to make synthetic aviation fuel.

The agreement with Siemens Energy completes the project's core partner set-up, adding to a list already including Spanish engineering company Tecnicas Reunidas, which is leading the front-end engineering design (FEED), and technology partners Topsoe and Sasol.

The partners will work on refining the plant design, cost estimates and implementation schedule ahead of the FID.
